clue.text: Good authors initially shared stories in abundance

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the two words before it

blocks.note: the opening letters of the two words
lore is the body of tales and knowledge a community passes around

explanation.surface: Talented writers once swapped plenty of tales with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: GA plus LORE gives GALORE; galore conventionally follows its noun, as in 'prizes galore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore is an adverb-like word meaning in plentiful quantity, a straight synonym for plentifully.

clue.text: Removes an insult (possibly extremely libellous)

indicators.note: possibly suggests the words are only one arrangement of many, so the letters may be reordered
extremely refers to the extremes, the two end letters of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone deletes a defamatory remark that might well have been libellous.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes 'possibly extremely libellous' look like a legal aside about the insult, but it holds both the anagram signal and the two extra letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To uninstall software is to take it off a computer, so the verb matches removes in computing contexts.

clue.text: A fruity pastry’s inverted layers

indicators.note: in a down entry, inverted means turned upside down, so the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a fruit tart is a fruity pastry, with the possessive supplying the S

explanation.surface: An upside-down fruit pastry shows its separate tiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A TART'S written backwards gives STRATA; the apostrophe S is read as part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are horizontal bands of rock or tiers within a structure, the plural noun matching layers.

clue.text: Frame of roadhouse underpinned by aluminium and concrete

indicators.note: the frame is the border, meaning the outside letters of the next word only
in a down entry, being underpinned means something else sits below, so the next piece follows underneath

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A roadside inn is built with a metal frame resting on a concrete base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like more building material, but it is the definition in its adjective sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete as an adjective means actual and tangible rather than abstract, which is what real describes.

clue.text: Plant area headed by horrible person

indicators.note: in a down entry, being headed by something puts that other piece on top, so it comes first

blocks.note: a monster is a cruel or horrible person
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A district is run by someone thoroughly nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant name is spelt with the person first and the area letter beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstera is a tropical climbing genus, the Swiss cheese plant popular as a houseplant.

clue.text: Awaiting endless details

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

blocks.note: to be in for something is to have it coming, to await it

explanation.surface: Someone is waiting for particulars that never stop coming.
explanation.walkthrough: IN FOR loses its last letter to leave INFO.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, meaning facts or particulars about something.

clue.text: Colour match with an outline of felt tip, perhaps

indicators.note: an outline is drawn around a shape, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: a felt tip is one example of a pen, signalled by perhaps
two accounts match when they agree

explanation.surface: Choosing a shade to match, with a felt tip outlining it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a noun to pair with the colour, but it is a verb here, and the felt tip is the outer casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a yellowish-green shade named after garden peas, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Doctor in Perth wanted to have a wild celebration

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician in Perth fancied a big night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person in Perth, but it is a verb telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint the town red is an idiom for going out and partying riotously.

clue.text: Ultimately had to show determination following total collapse

indicators.note: ultimately points at the closing letter of each of the four words that follow
here following is not position but a word in its own right, standing for its usual abbreviation

blocks.note: the final letters of the four words
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the total is the whole, all of it

explanation.surface: In the end someone had to dig in after a complete breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show determination' looks like a phrase to define, but its words only lend their last letters; F for following comes from references like 'p. 12 f.'.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a sudden ruin or fall from power, the noun sense of collapse.

clue.text: Butt of jokes seems too generic in part

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is needed, a run of letters spanning the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the next two

explanation.surface: A comic's target is criticised as rather bland in places.
explanation.walkthrough: Look across seemS TOO GEneric.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a comedian's sidekick who is the target of the jokes, so a butt of them.

clue.text: Counteract a spread of stale urine

indicators.note: something spread is scattered about, so its letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for dealing with a puddle of old urine.
explanation.definitionFit: To neutralise something is to cancel out its effect, the same verb sense as to offset it.

clue.text: Part of karabiner that’s not moving

indicators.note: only a portion of the words that follow is wanted, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A climber notices one bit of the clip is stuck fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Look across karabINER That; a karabiner is a climber's spring clip.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless or lacking the power to move, a direct synonym for stationary.

clue.text: Creative output is almost perfect

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter falls away

blocks.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A judgement that a piece of creative work is nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a product of the imagination, something a creative mind generates and puts forward.

clue.text: Gift Aid regularly accepted by one home-grown scheme

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
what is accepted is taken in, so it goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
native means originating locally
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A local charity scheme takes in donations through Gift Aid.
explanation.walkthrough: Gift Aid is a UK scheme letting charities reclaim tax on donations; here its name only lends alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiative is a new plan or programme launched to tackle something, so a scheme.

clue.text: Corporate communication efforts somehow capture billions

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Corporate messaging campaigns manage to rake in huge sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capture' looks like a container signal around B for billions, but both words are simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Public relations is the business work of managing a company's image and messages to outsiders.

clue.text: What bad companies may do is trivialise losing pounds

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so a letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: to underplay something is to make it seem less important
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Bad firms might shrug off money matters as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDERPLAY drops its L to leave UNDERPAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor employers pay staff too little, and the verb for giving workers less than fair wages is this.

clue.text: Compact cupboard containing empty suitcase

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other
emptied of its contents, the word keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: a closet is a cupboard
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A small cupboard has an unpacked suitcase stored inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compact' looks like a description of the cupboard, but it is the definition, in its adjective sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-set means placed tightly together, like close-set eyes, so it is a synonym for dense or compressed.

clue.text: Fondness periodically produces laudatory works

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Affection now and then inspires poems of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems written in praise of their subject, so they are works that extol.

clue.text: Wearing camouflage, say, is marvellous!

blocks.note: first meaning: hidden from view, which camouflage is one way to be
second meaning: dated slang for wonderful, like far out

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as praising someone's camouflage; the literal and the slang senses are the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means unseen, and in 1960s slang it meant excellent or fantastic.

clue.text: Likely to get riled about new, expensive clothes?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a fiery person has a quick temper
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Would someone be annoyed by pricey new outfits?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the whimsical surface; 'about' sits between the two pieces it joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Finery is showy, elegant dress worn for special occasions, so costly attire.

clue.text: Drinking establishment in chic port city

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: hot can mean fashionable
a bar is a place to drink

explanation.surface: A trendy pub in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobart is the capital of Tasmania, Australia, on the Derwent estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is a harbour city with a busy waterfront, an example of a port city.

clue.text: Rowing teams picked up for boat trip

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on a radio, so the word is taken by sound

blocks.note: rowing teams are crews

explanation.surface: Rowers are collected for an outing on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure voyage on a ship, a journey by water taken for leisure.

clue.text: Repulsive king, very unfriendly on the outside

indicators.note: being on the outside means wrapping round, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: an icy manner is very cold and unfriendly
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A disgusting monarch who is frosty to everyone on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the outside' reads as the king's outward manner, but it tells you the coldness wraps round the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky is informal for nasty or distasteful, causing disgust in the same way as revolting.

clue.text: Fan frenzy carrying to Britain and somewhere in Canada

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the following pieces go inside

blocks.note: mania is a craze or wild enthusiasm
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for Britain

explanation.surface: Excited supporters bring their fervour over to Britain and to a Canadian location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' tempts as an anagram of something, but 'Fan frenzy' together is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is a prairie province of central Canada, so it is a place within that country.

clue.text: Small part of vehicle check close to engine

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for cars
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mechanic inspects a small component near the motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to engine' reads as a location near the engine, but it means that word's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mote is a tiny particle, such as a speck of dust, so it is a minute piece.

clue.text: Ones offering unsolicited advice to support new advertisers

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the following letters are made over

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Consultants with uninvited opinions are hired to help fresh advertising firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Back-seat drivers are passengers who keep telling the driver what to do, and by extension any interfering critics.
